chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Hāshim, from Abū Khadījah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

It is not permissible for two women to spend the night in one blanket unless there is a barrier between them. If they do so, they are to be forbidden from that; and if they are found after the prohibition, each one of them is to be flogged with a hadd punishment. Then if they are found again in one blanket, they are flogged; and if they are found a third time, they are killed.

key_terms.حَاجِزٌ: a barrier or separator between the two
key_terms.قُتِلَتَا: the two are put to death
key_terms.لِحَافٍ: a blanket or shared covering used for sleeping
key_terms.نُهِيَتَا: the two are prohibited or warned against the act

ai.seo_question: What does Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām say about two women sleeping under one blanket?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a legal ruling concerning two women sleeping together under one blanket without a barrier between them. It outlines escalating punishment after warning and repeated offense, reflecting the severity assigned in this chapter to acts associated with siḥāq.
